text:
The distance from the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) to the Milky Way is about  
\(L \approx 1.6\times10^{5}\) ly (≈ 158 000–163 000 ly).  

The spacecraft’s speed is  

\[
\beta = \frac{v}{c}=0.99999987 = 1-\delta,\qquad \delta = 1.3\times10^{-7}.
\]

For a ultra‑relativistic speed  

\[
\gamma = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-\beta^{2}}}\approx\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\delta}}
      =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2(1.3\times10^{-7})}}
      \approx 1.96\times10^{3}.
\]

**Time in Earth’s frame**

Because \(c=1\;\text{ly yr}^{-1}\),

\[
t_{\text{Earth}} = \frac{L}{v}\approx L\;(1+\delta) \approx 1.58\times10^{5}\ \text{yr}.
\]

**Proper (astronaut) time**

\[
\tau = \frac{t_{\text{Earth}}}{\gamma}
      \approx \frac{1.58\times10^{5}}{1.96\times10^{3}}
      \approx 8.0\times10^{1}\ \text{yr}\;\approx 81\ \text{yr}.
\]

The astronaut starts at age 22 yr, so after the trip he would be about  

\[
22\ \text{yr}+81\ \text{yr}\approx103\ \text{yr},
\]

well below the species‑average lifespan of 150 yr. Hence he will survive the journey.

Thus the travel time measured by the astronaut is roughly 81 years.

**Answer: A**.
